To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reaction of a “double salt” with trifluoroacetanhydride yields several novel polyheteroaromatic compounds.

the reaction of tetraaminopyridine hydrochloride with tin(II) chloride and trifluoroacetylation of the resulting tetraamino‐tin “double salt” leads to the formation of 2,7‐bis(trifluor‐omethyl)-1‐,3‐,6‐,8‐tetraazapyrene and its heterocyclic derivatives.

the reaction between the tin “double salts” of tetraamino-2,7-difluoronaphthalene hydrobromide with trifluoromethanesulfonic acid or trifluoroacetyl chloride in pyridine affords 2,7-dihalogeno-1,3,8,10-tetraazadibenzotriquinacene (DBTQ) derivatives in moderate to high yields.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel heterocyclic compounds with a high degree of aromaticity and a large number of conjugated π electrons.
the development and application of novel polyheterocyclic compounds for the construction of organic materials with tailored electronic, optical, and redox properties.
the development and application of novel polyheteroaromatic systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reaction of the “double salt” with TFAA in pyridine leads to a variety of products, some of which are of considerable interest for further investigations.

the reaction of tetraaminopyridine with trifluoroacetate anhydride leads to the expected 2,7‐bis(trifluoromet)‐1,3,8‐tetraazapyrene and to the formation of several new heteroaromatic compounds as a result of a [3+2] cycloaddition of the tetraaminopyrylium intermediate with a furan or indolizidine unit.

the reaction of 1,2,4,5-tetraaminonaphthyltin hydrochloride with CF3CO2H in pyridine yields the expected 1,3-difluoro derivative 1, but also a series of novel heterocycles that were formed by the addition of a furan or indolizinium ring to the TAP core.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reaction of the “double salt” with trifluoro-acetic anhydric is a very useful method for the preparation of a broad range of polyheterocycles.
the reaction of the “double salt” with trifluoro acetic anhydrides leads to several interesting heterocyclic compounds, which can be obtained in good yield.

the reaction of tetraaminopyridine hydrochloride with tin tetrachloride and trifluoroacetyl chloride leads to the formation of the tin “doubly” complexed 1,3-diaminopyridinium salt, which reacts with trifluoroacetate anions in the presence of pyridine to form the trifluoroacetamidopyridines.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the annulation of electron-rich heterocyclic moieties to TAPy may lead to the isolation of unexpected heterocycles, and that the electronic properties of the resulting molecules can be tuned by varying the heterocycle.
1,3-oxazin-6-ones are not inert towards nucleophiles, but can undergo nucleophilic ring opening.

the tin “double salts” of tetraaminoarenes are useful starting materials for the preparation of polyheterocyclic compounds, which are otherwise inaccessible by direct reaction of tetraaminobenzenes with trifluoroacetimidoyl chloride.
